title: Three for One, Same Total: Jordan Sells Jeanty to Alan, and the Math Comes Out Even Except Where It Doesn't
dek: Jordan turned Ashton Jeanty into Isaiah Likely, Emeka Egbuka and Denzel Boston, a deal that balanced to within half a point on the stat sheet and still cost Team Pillbert five points of title odds.
body: The league's third trade of 2026 is a three-for-one. Before Week 5, Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV sent running back Ashton Jeanty to Alan's Team Pillbert for tight end Isaiah Likely and wide receivers Emeka Egbuka and Denzel Boston. On the stat sheet it is almost perfectly balanced: Jeanty had 64.4 points through four weeks, and the three players coming back to Jordan had 64.8 combined. Jordan technically won the raw-points exchange by 0.4, which is the first thing he has won all season.

That even split hides a big difference in how the points were made. Jeanty scored all 64.4 in four weeks on one roster, about 16.1 a game, the kind of steady volume that wins weekly matchups. Jordan's new trio got there in pieces. Egbuka has 28.6 in four weeks on a roster, about 7.2 a week. Likely has 18.2 in three weeks, about 6.1. Boston has 18 in just two weeks, a 9-point-per-week pace that is the most interesting number in the package. Three roster spots of solid-but-unspectacular production for one workhorse is a classic depth-for-star swap, and Jordan took the depth.

For Counting or not Counting GV, the model's verdict is the shortest possible review: 0% title odds before, 0% after. At 0-4 with a league-low 349.2 points, Jordan is not trading for this year's trophy so much as for more bodies to start each Sunday, and three starters beat one when your lineup has holes everywhere. He has been busy on the wire too, adding Kirk Cousins, Dalton Schultz and Michael Wilson. The rebuild does not move the needle yet, but it does at least give him more ways to score.

Alan's side is the puzzling one. Team Pillbert entered the trade riding a three-game winning streak and 21% title odds, then picked up the best player in the deal and came out at 16%. The likeliest explanation is that the model thinks losing a tight end and two receivers thinned Alan's lineup more than Jeanty filled it. The bigger tell is what Alan did next: he immediately flipped Jeanty and Davante Adams to Mekhi for Justin Jefferson. That makes this deal look less like a destination and more like a layover, with Jeanty as the currency for the receiver Alan actually wanted.

So who won on paper? By the title odds, Jordan, if only because a team at 0% cannot lose any ground and Alan gave up five points getting here. By the plan, the jury waits on Week 5, when Alan visits Mekhi's Dawgs and has to watch Jeanty line up against him, while Jordan faces Zoe and tries to get Egbuka, Likely and Boston to deliver his first win. Paper says Jordan broke even and Alan paid a toll. The scoreboard gets the final say.

social.author: Spreadsheet Steve
social.text: Jeanty: 64.4 points. Likely + Egbuka + Boston: 64.8 points. Jordan won this trade by 0.4 and I will not be taking questions.

social.author: Pillbert Nation
social.text: Down 5 points of title odds for a guy we flipped about five minutes later? Relax. That was the toll road to Justin Jefferson. Ask us after Week 5.

social.author: GV Counting Club
social.text: 0% before. 0% after. Three new starters, a Boston who's averaging 9 a week, and nowhere to go but up. The rebuild is counting, and it counts.

social.author: Buckaroo Insider
social.text: Sources say Mekhi has circled Week 5 on his calendar. Alan sold Jeanty to him, and now gets to watch Jeanty from the other sideline.

social.author: The Depth Chart Doc
social.text: One RB at 16.1 a game for three guys between 6 and 9 a week. Classic stars-and-scrubs vs. depth debate, and the model sided with nobody.
